---
title: "Predictive model"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: across species, is the subadult - adult contrast phylogenetically structured, or related
to habitat breadth, aquatic habit or an extended larval period (Q7)? Replaces
`size_bd_unified/05_species_regression.qmd` (built on m11g, retired 2026-11-25). Specification
and reasons: `README.md` "Downstream models" -> "Predictive model".

In short:

- **response**: each species' mean contrast from stage 1 (prevalence and load in one
  multivariate model, so their phylogenetic correlation is estimated), with its posterior sd as
  a known standard error. Tier D species get an inflated se (`03`).
- **predictors**: log habitat breadth and aquatic index (standardized), extended larval period
  (age at metamorphosis > 12 months, overwintering larvae; 8 of 31 species), and a phylogenetic
  random effect.
- **fits**:
  - *main*: stage 1 mean contrasts, all species (31 prevalence, 30 load)
  - *same-condition* (sensitivity): species contrasts from co-sampled events only (`04`; 22 /
    15 species). Every species then contributes the same kind of contrast (README "How to read
    the results", "As-sampled contrasts"). Prevalence from the binomial model on co-sampled
    events, load from the empirical event contrasts (2026-11-27; see the Data chunk)
  - *same-condition, empirical* (comparison): as above with the empirical prevalence logits,
    which the Haldane ceiling compresses (kept to show the estimator's effect)
  - *check*: main + the share of swabs in co-sampled events (that part's definition). Its slope
    near 0 = the same-condition / realized mix does not shift contrasts systematically
  - *ordinal* (sensitivity): age at metamorphosis as an ordered predictor (D < R < M < E) with a
    monotonic effect; only its total effect is readable (D and R hold 1 and 2 species)

Reading: posterior medians with 50 / 95% intervals and pd. With 31 species, slopes will be
uncertain; a wide interval centered near 0 means "not informed", not "no effect".

Run order: `01_contrast_tiers.Rmd`, `03_contrast_analysis.Rmd` (writes
`03_predictive_responses.csv`), `04_contrast_environment_screen.qmd` (writes
`04_same_condition_species_contrasts.csv`), then this script. Fits are small (seconds to minutes)
and cached with `file =`.

# Setup
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, posterior, tidybayes, ape, priorsense, ggrepel)

intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")
models_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "models", "predictive")
dir.create(models_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# conv_check() (shared with the other brms analyses)
source(here("size_bd_season", "season_check_functions.R"))

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

```

# Data
```{r}
# responses: one row per species x part
#   stage 1 (03): contrast_mean, contrast_sd, contrast_se (tier D inflated), tier,
#                 pct_swabs_co_event (share of swabs in co-sampled events, part definition)
#   same-condition (04): contrast_mean, contrast_sd from co-sampled events only
#     prevalence: binomial model on the co-sampled events' counts (no ceiling; event-varying
#                 contrasts). the empirical logits (Haldane-corrected, per event) are capped near
#                 +/- 2.4 in small all-or-nothing cells and came out compressed (r. sierrae 0.39
#                 vs 0.81 binomial vs 0.99 stage 1); kept as a labelled comparison
#     load:       empirical event contrasts (no ceiling problem; agreed with stage 1)
responses_main = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_predictive_responses.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)
responses_sc_empirical = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "04_same_condition_species_contrasts.csv"),
                                  show_col_types = FALSE)
responses_sc = bind_rows(
  read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "04_binomial_prevalence_contrasts.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(part = "prevalence"),
  responses_sc_empirical %>% filter(part == "load"))

# traits. habitat breadth and aquatic index: IUCN habitat metrics (as in the unified 05).
# age at metamorphosis: species notes (D direct, R < 2 months, M 2-12 months, E > 12 months;
# codings for r. catesbeiana, r. clamitans and h. phyllodes fixed 2026-11-26). the first data row
# of the notes file holds the code legend, so rows without a species are dropped
habitat = read_csv(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "iucn_habitat_metrics.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, habitat_breadth, aquatic_index)

species_notes = read_csv(here("data", "species_notes_2026-11-26.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE,
                         name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
  filter(!is.na(species)) %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture = species, age_metamorphosis = `Age at Metamorphosis`)

traits = habitat %>%
  inner_join(species_notes, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% responses_main$taxon_capture)

# every species with a response needs traits (expected: none missing)
setdiff(unique(responses_main$taxon_capture), traits$taxon_capture)

# predictors, scaled once over the main species set (reused in every fit):
#   log_hb_z         log habitat breadth, standardized (per sd)
#   aquatic_z        aquatic index, standardized (per sd)
#   extended_larval  +0.5 extended larval period (E), -0.5 otherwise: the slope is the difference
#                    between the two groups, the intercept their midpoint (as stage_c in stage 1)
#   age_met_ord      ordered factor D < R < M < E for the monotonic variant
traits = traits %>%
  mutate(log_hb_z = as.numeric(scale(log(habitat_breadth))),
         aquatic_z = as.numeric(scale(aquatic_index)),
         extended_larval = if_else(age_metamorphosis == "E", 0.5, -0.5),
         age_met_ord = factor(age_metamorphosis, levels = c("D", "R", "M", "E"), ordered = TRUE))

traits %>% count(age_metamorphosis)

# predictor correlations (31 species): high values make separate slopes uncertain
round(cor(traits %>% transmute(log_hb_z, aquatic_z, extended_larval)), 2)

# phylogenetic correlation matrix (diag = 1, so the phylogenetic sd is on the same scale as
# sigma and their ratio reads as a phylogenetic signal), pruned to the species modeled
phylo_tree = read.tree(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "phylo_tree.nwk"))
setdiff(traits$taxon_capture, phylo_tree$tip.label)   # expected: none
phylo_tree = keep.tip(phylo_tree, traits$taxon_capture)
A = vcv.phylo(phylo_tree, corr = TRUE)

# wide data for the multivariate model: one row per species, one response column per part.
# a part a species lacks (e.g. b. faber load) is excluded with subset(); its response and se are
# filled with placeholders (0, 1) so brms does not drop the whole row
make_wide = function(responses, se_col) {
  responses %>%
    transmute(taxon_capture, part, y = contrast_mean, se = .data[[se_col]],
              share_z = if ("pct_swabs_co_event" %in% names(responses)) pct_swabs_co_event else NA_real_) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(y, se, share_z), names_glue = "{part}_{.value}") %>%
    rename(prevalence = prevalence_y, load = load_y) %>%
    mutate(has_prevalence = !is.na(prevalence), has_load = !is.na(load),
           across(c(prevalence, load), ~ coalesce(.x, 0)),
           across(c(prevalence_se, load_se), ~ coalesce(.x, 1))) %>%
    left_join(traits, by = "taxon_capture")
}

data_main = make_wide(responses_main, "contrast_se") %>%
  # check-fit predictor: share of swabs in co-sampled events, standardized within each part
  mutate(prevalence_share_z = as.numeric(scale(prevalence_share_z)),
         load_share_z = if_else(has_load, as.numeric(scale(if_else(has_load, load_share_z, NA_real_))), 0))
data_sc = make_wide(responses_sc, "contrast_sd")
data_sc_empirical = make_wide(responses_sc_empirical, "contrast_sd")

data_main %>% summarise(n_species = n(), n_prevalence = sum(has_prevalence), n_load = sum(has_load))
data_sc %>% summarise(n_species = n(), n_prevalence = sum(has_prevalence), n_load = sum(has_load))

```

# Model
```{r}
# one formula per part:
#   y | se(se, sigma = TRUE)   y ~ N(mu, sqrt(sigma^2 + se^2)): se = the species' known
#                              estimation error; sigma = species variation beyond it that is not
#                              phylogenetic
#   + subset(has_*)            species without that part are left out of it
#   (1 | p | gr(taxon_capture, cov = A))
#                              phylogenetic effect (species correlated by shared ancestry); the
#                              shared "p" estimates the correlation between the prevalence and
#                              load effects
# rescor = FALSE: no residual correlation (not identifiable with known se)
predictive_bf = function(part, rhs) {
  bf(as.formula(paste0(part, " | se(", part, "_se, sigma = TRUE) + subset(has_", part, ") ~ ",
                       rhs, " + (1 | p | gr(taxon_capture, cov = A))")))
}

rhs_main = "1 + log_hb_z + aquatic_z + extended_larval"
rhs_ord = "1 + log_hb_z + aquatic_z + mo(age_met_ord)"

formula_main = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", rhs_main), predictive_bf("load", rhs_main), rescor = FALSE)
formula_check = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", paste(rhs_main, "+ prevalence_share_z")),
                     predictive_bf("load", paste(rhs_main, "+ load_share_z")), rescor = FALSE)
formula_ord = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", rhs_ord), predictive_bf("load", rhs_ord), rescor = FALSE)

# priors, on the contrast scale (prevalence: logit; load: log load among positives):
#   intercepts normal(0, 2) / normal(0, 3), as the stage 1 mean contrasts
#   slopes normal(0, 1): a one-sd change in a trait (or extended vs not) shifting the mean
#     contrast by more than ~2 units is implausible
#   phylogenetic sd and sigma exponential(1); correlation lkj(2)
# the monotonic variant's step proportions keep brms' default dirichlet(1)
predictive_priors = c(
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 3)", class = "Intercept", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor"))

fit_predictive = function(formula, data, name) {
  brm(formula, data = data, data2 = list(A = A[data$taxon_capture, data$taxon_capture]),
      family = gaussian(), prior = predictive_priors,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
      chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
      file = file.path(models_dir, name), file_refit = "on_change")
}

predictive_fits = list(
  main           = fit_predictive(formula_main,  data_main, "predictive_main"),
  same_condition = fit_predictive(formula_main,  data_sc,   "predictive_same_condition_binomial"),
  same_condition_empirical = fit_predictive(formula_main, data_sc_empirical, "predictive_same_condition"),
  check          = fit_predictive(formula_check, data_main, "predictive_check"),
  ordinal        = fit_predictive(formula_ord,   data_main, "predictive_ordinal"))

# sampler checks (thresholds in conv_check)
map_dfr(predictive_fits, conv_check, .id = "fit")

```

# Checks
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

# posterior predictive check per part (main fit): the spread of species contrasts the model
# expects vs the observed means
map(c("prevalence", "load"), ~ pp_check(predictive_fits$main, resp = .x, ndraws = 100) +
      ggtitle(.x))

# prior sensitivity (power-scaling; small model, so the full check is cheap): "prior" > 0.05 on
# a slope = it follows its prior more than the data (expected for weakly informed traits)
# brms computes the log-likelihood of a multivariate model with subset() one response at a time
# (passing the brmsfit to priorsense fails), so the draws are built here as in
# 02_contrast_modeling.qmd: the parameters, the log prior terms (lprior*), and the log-likelihood
# summed over species and both responses. power-scaling only needs that per-draw sum
fit_ps = predictive_fits$main
ps_vars = grep("^(b|sd|sigma)_", variables(fit_ps), value = TRUE)
ps_draws = as_draws_df(fit_ps, variable = c(ps_vars, grep("^lprior", variables(fit_ps), value = TRUE)))
ps_draws$log_lik = rowSums(log_lik(fit_ps, resp = "prevalence")) +
  rowSums(log_lik(fit_ps, resp = "load"))
powerscale_sensitivity(ps_draws, variable = ps_vars) %>%
  filter(diagnosis != "-")

```

# Results
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

# trait slopes per fit: change in the mean contrast per sd of the trait (log habitat breadth,
# aquatic index, co-sampling share), or between extended and other larval periods. median,
# 50 / 95% intervals, pd
slope_draws = imap_dfr(predictive_fits, function(fit, name) {
  as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b|bsp)_(prevalence|load)_", regex = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    select(starts_with("b"), -contains("Intercept")) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(fit = name,
           part = str_match(parameter, "_(prevalence|load)_")[, 2],
           term = sub("^(b|bsp)_(prevalence|load)_", "", parameter))
})

(slope_summary = slope_draws %>%
  group_by(fit, part, term) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value),
            lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
            lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(part, term, fit))

# main vs same-condition vs check, the shared terms: agreement = trait conclusions do not rest on
# the same-condition / realized mix
slope_draws %>%
  filter(fit %in% c("main", "same_condition", "same_condition_empirical", "check"),
         term %in% c("log_hb_z", "aquatic_z", "extended_larval")) %>%
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("check", "same_condition_empirical", "same_condition", "main"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = term, color = fit)) +
  stat_pointinterval(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(part = c(prevalence = "prevalence (logit)", load = "load among positives (log)"))) +
  labs(x = "change in the mean contrast (median, 50 / 95%)", y = NULL, color = "fit",
       subtitle = "per sd of log habitat breadth / aquatic index; extended_larval = extended - other") +
  theme_classic()

```

## Phylogenetic signal and the prevalence - load correlation
```{r}
# phylogenetic signal per part: sd_phylo^2 / (sd_phylo^2 + sigma^2), the share of species
# variation beyond estimation error that follows the phylogeny (reads like Pagel's lambda, since
# A is a correlation matrix). with ~31 species the two sds are only partly separable, so expect
# wide intervals. cor_p = correlation of the phylogenetic effects on the prevalence and load
# contrasts
signal_summary = imap_dfr(predictive_fits[c("main", "same_condition")], function(fit, name) {
  dr = as_draws_df(fit) %>% as_tibble()
  tibble(.draw = dr$.draw,
         h2_prevalence = dr$sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept^2 /
           (dr$sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept^2 + dr$sigma_prevalence^2),
         h2_load = dr$sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept^2 /
           (dr$sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept^2 + dr$sigma_load^2),
         cor_prevalence_load = dr$cor_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept__load_Intercept) %>%
    pivot_longer(-.draw, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(fit = name)
}) %>%
  group_by(fit, metric) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value),
            lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
            lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))

signal_summary

```

## Better-informed versions of the signal and the correlation
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

# with 31 species the phylogenetic sd and sigma are only partly separable, so the residual H2
# and the phylogenetic prevalence - load correlation above are not informed. four better-defined
# questions and checks (added 2026-11-27):
#   (1) raw phylogenetic signal: an intercept-only model (no traits). Q7 asks whether the contrast
#       is phylogenetically structured; the traits are clustered (6 of 8 extended species are
#       rana), so the H2 above is what is left after them
#   (2) prior vs posterior: how much the data reshape H2 and the correlation
#   (3) total cross-species correlation: phylogenetic + non-phylogenetic species effects, both
#       correlated across the parts (the non-phylogenetic effect replaces sigma)
#   (4) predictive value of the phylogeny: loo with vs without the phylogenetic effect
# plus the within-species estimation-error check (from 03)

# H2 and the phylogenetic correlation of one fit, per draw (models with sigma)
signal_draws_of = function(fit, name) {
  dr = as_draws_df(fit) %>% as_tibble()
  tibble(.draw = dr$.draw,
         h2_prevalence = dr$sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept^2 /
           (dr$sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept^2 + dr$sigma_prevalence^2),
         h2_load = dr$sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept^2 /
           (dr$sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept^2 + dr$sigma_load^2),
         cor_phylo = dr$cor_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept__load_Intercept) %>%
    pivot_longer(-.draw, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(fit = name)
}
summarise_metric = function(draws) {
  draws %>%
    group_by(fit, metric) %>%
    summarise(median = median(value),
              lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
              lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
              pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
}

# (1) intercept-only phylogenetic model
formula_phylo_only = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", "1"), predictive_bf("load", "1"), rescor = FALSE)
priors_no_b = predictive_priors[predictive_priors$class != "b", ]
fit_phylo_only = brm(formula_phylo_only, data = data_main,
                     data2 = list(A = A[data_main$taxon_capture, data_main$taxon_capture]),
                     family = gaussian(), prior = priors_no_b,
                     control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
                     chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
                     file = file.path(models_dir, "predictive_phylo_only"), file_refit = "on_change")
conv_check(fit_phylo_only)

# (2) the priors these imply: the sds are exponential(1) each, so H2 = a^2 / (a^2 + b^2) with
# a, b ~ exponential(1); the lkj(2) correlation of a 2 x 2 matrix has (r + 1) / 2 ~ beta(2, 2)
set.seed(128)
n_prior = 16000
prior_draws = tibble(.draw = seq_len(n_prior),
                     a = rexp(n_prior, 1), b = rexp(n_prior, 1),
                     h2 = a^2 / (a^2 + b^2),
                     cor_phylo = 2 * rbeta(n_prior, 2, 2) - 1)
prior_signal = bind_rows(
  prior_draws %>% transmute(.draw, metric = "h2_prevalence", value = h2),
  prior_draws %>% transmute(.draw, metric = "h2_load", value = h2),
  prior_draws %>% transmute(.draw, metric = "cor_phylo", value = cor_phylo)) %>%
  mutate(fit = "prior")

signal_compare = bind_rows(prior_signal,
                           signal_draws_of(fit_phylo_only, "phylo_only (no traits)"),
                           signal_draws_of(predictive_fits$main, "main (traits)"))

(signal_compare_summary = summarise_metric(signal_compare))

signal_compare %>%
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("prior", "phylo_only (no traits)", "main (traits)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, color = fit, fill = fit)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.15, adjust = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "density", color = NULL, fill = NULL,
       subtitle = "posterior vs prior: a posterior that matches its prior = not informed") +
  theme_classic()

# (3) total cross-species correlation: phylogenetic (p) and non-phylogenetic (q) species
# effects, each correlated across the parts; se() without sigma (the q effect takes its role).
# total correlation per draw = (cov_p + cov_q) / sqrt(total var prevalence x total var load)
predictive_bf_total = function(part, rhs) {
  bf(as.formula(paste0(part, " | se(", part, "_se) + subset(has_", part, ") ~ ", rhs,
                       " + (1 | p | gr(taxon_capture, cov = A)) + (1 | q | taxon_id)")))
}
data_total = data_main %>% mutate(taxon_id = taxon_capture)   # second grouping column for q
formula_total = mvbf(predictive_bf_total("prevalence", rhs_main), predictive_bf_total("load", rhs_main),
                     rescor = FALSE)
priors_total = predictive_priors[predictive_priors$class != "sigma", ]
fit_total = brm(formula_total, data = data_total,
                data2 = list(A = A[data_total$taxon_capture, data_total$taxon_capture]),
                family = gaussian(), prior = priors_total,
                control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
                chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
                file = file.path(models_dir, "predictive_total_cor"), file_refit = "on_change")
conv_check(fit_total)

total_cor_draws = as_draws_df(fit_total) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  transmute(.draw,
            sp_p = sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept, sl_p = sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept,
            r_p = cor_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept__load_Intercept,
            sp_q = sd_taxon_id__prevalence_Intercept, sl_q = sd_taxon_id__load_Intercept,
            r_q = cor_taxon_id__prevalence_Intercept__load_Intercept,
            value = (r_p * sp_p * sl_p + r_q * sp_q * sl_q) /
              sqrt((sp_p^2 + sp_q^2) * (sl_p^2 + sl_q^2))) %>%
  transmute(.draw, metric = "cor_total", value, fit = "total (phylo + non-phylo)")

(total_cor_summary = summarise_metric(total_cor_draws))

# within-species estimation-error correlation (03): near 0 supports treating the two parts'
# errors as independent in se()
error_cor_file = file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_predictive_error_cor.csv")
if (file.exists(error_cor_file)) {
  error_cor = read_csv(error_cor_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  print(summary(error_cor$error_cor))
  print(error_cor %>% filter(abs(error_cor) > 0.2))
} else {
  message("no ", error_cor_file, ": re-run 03_contrast_analysis.Rmd")
}

# (4) predictive value of the phylogeny: the main model without the phylogenetic effect,
# compared by loo per part (one response at a time, as brms requires with subset())
predictive_bf_no_phylo = function(part, rhs) {
  bf(as.formula(paste0(part, " | se(", part, "_se, sigma = TRUE) + subset(has_", part, ") ~ ", rhs)))
}
formula_no_phylo = mvbf(predictive_bf_no_phylo("prevalence", rhs_main),
                        predictive_bf_no_phylo("load", rhs_main), rescor = FALSE)
priors_no_phylo = predictive_priors[!predictive_priors$class %in% c("sd", "cor"), ]
fit_no_phylo = brm(formula_no_phylo, data = data_main, family = gaussian(), prior = priors_no_phylo,
                   control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
                   chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
                   file = file.path(models_dir, "predictive_no_phylo"), file_refit = "on_change")
conv_check(fit_no_phylo)

# elpd difference per part: negative for no_phylo = the phylogeny improves prediction of a
# held-out species' contrast; |difference| < ~2 se = no clear difference
(loo_phylo = map_dfr(c("prevalence", "load"), function(part) {
  comp = loo_compare(list(with_phylo = loo(predictive_fits$main, resp = part),
                          no_phylo = loo(fit_no_phylo, resp = part)))
  as_tibble(comp, rownames = "model") %>%
    transmute(part = part, model, elpd_diff = round(elpd_diff, 2), se_diff = round(se_diff, 2))
}))

```

# Robustness of the main result
The same-condition fit with empirical prevalence logits shrank the extended-larval and
(prevalence) habitat-breadth slopes. Three explanations, separated here (added 2026-11-26):

1. **species set**: the same-condition fit lacks 9 species with no co-sampled events (all
   non-extended). -> the main model refit on exactly the same-condition species.
2. **estimand**: part of the effect is timing (realized, not same-condition contrasts). -> the
   species-level comparison of the two contrasts.
3. **noisier, compressed response**: empirical event contrasts and the Haldane correction pull
   large prevalence contrasts toward 0. -> also visible in the species comparison.

Result (2026-11-27): the species set was not the reason for prevalence (main on the
same-condition species: extended larval period +1.40 vs +1.43) but was for load (+0.79 vs
+1.34). For prevalence the estimator was most of it: the binomial model on co-sampled events
(`04`) is close to stage 1 for most species (*R. sierrae* 0.81 vs 0.99), so the same-condition fit
now uses it. *R. muscosa* stays a real exception (0.30 vs 1.29): its stage 1 prevalence contrast
is mostly realized, carried by single-stage events.

Plus influence: with 8 extended species, one or two can carry the slope. -> Pareto k per species
and leave-one-out refits of each extended species (all 8, so the choice is not made after
looking at the results).

## Main model on the same-condition species
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

# trait slopes of one fit, long (helper for this section)
get_slopes = function(fit, name) {
  as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b|bsp)_(prevalence|load)_", regex = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    select(starts_with("b"), -contains("Intercept")) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(fit = name,
           part = str_match(parameter, "_(prevalence|load)_")[, 2],
           term = sub("^(b|bsp)_(prevalence|load)_", "", parameter))
}
summarise_slopes = function(draws, ...) {
  draws %>%
    group_by(..., part, term) %>%
    summarise(median = median(value),
              lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
              lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
              pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
}

# stage 1 responses, restricted per part to the species of the same-condition fit
data_matched = data_main %>%
  mutate(has_prevalence = has_prevalence & taxon_capture %in% data_sc$taxon_capture[data_sc$has_prevalence],
         has_load = has_load & taxon_capture %in% data_sc$taxon_capture[data_sc$has_load]) %>%
  filter(has_prevalence | has_load)

data_matched %>% summarise(n_species = n(), n_prevalence = sum(has_prevalence), n_load = sum(has_load))

fit_matched = fit_predictive(formula_main, data_matched, "predictive_main_matched")
conv_check(fit_matched)

# reading: main_matched close to main -> the species set is not the reason (estimand or noise);
# main_matched close to same_condition -> the species set is the reason
matched_draws = bind_rows(get_slopes(predictive_fits$main, "main"),
                          get_slopes(fit_matched, "main_matched"),
                          get_slopes(predictive_fits$same_condition, "same_condition"),
                          get_slopes(predictive_fits$same_condition_empirical, "same_condition_empirical"))

(matched_summary = summarise_slopes(matched_draws, fit) %>% arrange(part, term, fit))

matched_draws %>%
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("same_condition_empirical", "same_condition", "main_matched", "main"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = term, color = fit)) +
  stat_pointinterval(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "change in the mean contrast (median, 50 / 95%)", y = NULL, color = "fit",
       subtitle = "main = all species; main_matched = stage 1 contrasts of the same-condition species") +
  theme_classic()

```

## Stage 1 vs same-condition contrast, per species
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 12

# each species' stage 1 mean contrast (realized + same-condition mix) against its same-condition
# contrast (co-sampled events only), with 95% bars (mean +/- 1.96 sd). points on the 1:1 line:
# the two agree. extended species far below the line -> the extended effect is partly timing;
# large stage 1 prevalence contrasts pulled toward 0 -> compression (Haldane, empirical noise)
species_compare = responses_main %>%
  select(taxon_capture, part, tier, main_mean = contrast_mean, main_sd = contrast_sd) %>%
  inner_join(responses_sc %>% select(taxon_capture, part, sc_mean = contrast_mean, sc_sd = contrast_sd,
                                     n_events),
             by = c("taxon_capture", "part")) %>%
  left_join(traits %>% select(taxon_capture, age_metamorphosis), by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(larval_period = if_else(age_metamorphosis == "E", "extended", "other"),
         part = factor(part, levels = c("prevalence", "load")))

species_compare %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = main_mean, y = sc_mean, color = larval_period)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey85") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = sc_mean - 1.96 * sc_sd, ymax = sc_mean + 1.96 * sc_sd), width = 0, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = main_mean - 1.96 * main_sd, xmax = main_mean + 1.96 * main_sd), height = 0, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = taxon_capture), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "stage 1 mean contrast", y = "same-condition contrast (co-sampled events)",
       color = "larval period", subtitle = "95% bars; dashed = 1:1") +
  theme_classic()

# the extended - other difference in mean contrasts by source, among the species in both
# (unweighted means: a rough view, the models weight by se)
species_compare %>%
  group_by(part, larval_period) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), main = round(mean(main_mean), 2), same_condition = round(mean(sc_mean), 2),
            .groups = "drop")

```

## Influence
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10

# pareto k per species and part (main fit; loo one response at a time, as brms requires with
# subset()). k > 0.7: that species' contrast is poorly predicted from the others and influences
# the fit strongly
pareto_k = map_dfr(c("prevalence", "load"), function(part) {
  rows = data_main[[paste0("has_", part)]]
  lo = loo(predictive_fits$main, resp = part)
  tibble(taxon_capture = data_main$taxon_capture[rows], part = part,
         pareto_k = lo$diagnostics$pareto_k)
}) %>%
  left_join(traits %>% select(taxon_capture, age_metamorphosis), by = "taxon_capture")

pareto_k %>% arrange(desc(pareto_k)) %>% head(10)

# leave one extended species out (all 8): the extended-larval slope with each one dropped. a slope
# that stays away from 0 whichever species is dropped does not rest on a single species
extended_species = traits %>% filter(age_metamorphosis == "E") %>% pull(taxon_capture)

loso_draws = map_dfr(extended_species, function(sp) {
  fit = fit_predictive(formula_main, data_main %>% filter(taxon_capture != sp),
                       paste0("predictive_main_drop_", sp))
  get_slopes(fit, paste0("drop ", sp))
}) %>%
  bind_rows(get_slopes(predictive_fits$main, "main (all)")) %>%
  filter(term == "extended_larval")

(loso_summary = summarise_slopes(loso_draws, fit) %>% arrange(part, median))

loso_draws %>%
  mutate(fit = fct_relevel(fit, "main (all)", after = Inf)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = fit)) +
  stat_pointinterval(.width = c(0.5, 0.95)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "extended larval period slope (median, 50 / 95%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "main model with one extended species left out") +
  theme_classic()

```

## Without the time-segregated species
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 11

# why (2026-11-27): the main extended-larval effect leans partly on strongly negative stage 1
# contrasts of sparsely co-sampled, asynchronous species (e.g. p. crucifer -2.17,
# l. sphenocephalus -1.40), whose contrasts are largely realized and cannot be checked with
# within-event comparisons. (r. pipiens, -2.05, is weather-imbalanced but not time-segregated:
# 5 co-sampled events in 5 site-years, so it stays in this fit.) the time-segregated flag (01_contrast_tiers.Rmd; fewer
# co-sampled events than half the co-sampled site-years) was defined before any of this, so
# dropping the flagged species is a targeted, a priori sensitivity fit. no extended species is
# flagged, so the extended group stays whole.
# reading: extended slope near its main size -> the effect does not depend on the realized
# contrasts of the time-segregated species; much smaller -> it does.
# (synchrony is not used as a main covariate: the check fit already tests it as a linear term,
# and it is partly caused by life history, e.g. overwintering larvae, so adjusting for it would
# remove part of the trait effect)
species_table = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_species.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
time_segregated = species_table %>% filter(include, flag_time_segregated) %>% pull(taxon_capture)
time_segregated

data_no_tseg = data_main %>% filter(!taxon_capture %in% time_segregated)
data_no_tseg %>%
  summarise(n_species = n(), n_prevalence = sum(has_prevalence), n_load = sum(has_load),
            n_extended = sum(extended_larval > 0))

fit_no_tseg = fit_predictive(formula_main, data_no_tseg, "predictive_main_no_time_segregated")
conv_check(fit_no_tseg)

no_tseg_draws = bind_rows(get_slopes(predictive_fits$main, "main"),
                          get_slopes(fit_no_tseg, "main_no_time_segregated"))

(no_tseg_summary = summarise_slopes(no_tseg_draws, fit) %>% arrange(part, term, fit))

no_tseg_draws %>%
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("main_no_time_segregated", "main"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = term, color = fit)) +
  stat_pointinterval(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "change in the mean contrast (median, 50 / 95%)", y = NULL, color = "fit",
       subtitle = "main model with and without the 11 time-segregated species") +
  theme_classic()

```
